text:
Alex: Heads up — after the kernel-selection PR (#542) landed we see a ~25ms median regression on small chat requests (0–8 tokens). Looks concentrated in host-side parsing/tokenization + stream chunking path. Repro: curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/chat -d '{"input":"hi"}'

Jess: Ran quick local profiling. Flame snapshot:
```
total 120ms
parse_request: 2.1ms
http_body_read: 3.6ms
parse_json: 1.4ms
tokenize (host): 18.9ms
serialize_chunks: 5.2ms
rpc_send_copy: 22.0ms
```

Maya: I think rpc_send_copy is the big one. grpc gateway is doing two extra memcpy per chunk when we chunk/stream. For tiny requests the copies dominate. :thinking:

Ravi: Another wrinkle — we currently compute KV cache keys from tokenized prefix bytes. That means we tokenize first, even if the KV cache would be a full hit. If we instead compute a rolling hash on raw bytes we can bypass tokenize for cache hits.

Alex: Good point. That explains why KV hits aren't lowering latency here. Proposal: change KV key to be on canonicalized raw bytes (utf8-normalize + whitespace collapse) with a small fast rolling hash, then fallback to tokenize-based key when needed.

Jess: I prototyped a microbenchmark. patch branch: perf/stream-zero-copy. Microbench results (local, c5g.large-ish):
```
baseline median: 42.7ms
with zero-copy streaming: 30.4ms
delta: -12.3ms (29% improvement)
```

Maya: The change to kernel selection earlier re-ordered some initialization so the host path now does an extra buffer concat for every incoming chunk. That combined with grpc copies makes the worst-case 3x memcpy. We should either reorder init back or implement slice-view passing.

Ravi: Batching heuristic tweak: don't attempt to batch tiny requests under 16 tokens at the router level; serve them on the low-latency fast-path. For streaming clients, do an early accept and send to a single-worker path.

Alex: OK action items:
- Jess -> open canary PR for zero-copy streaming + revert small init reorder (PR #?)
- Ravi -> implement raw-bytes KV hashing prototype, add unit tests
- Maya -> add router fast-path for <=16 token requests and reduce buffer copies in http->grpc bridge
- Perf-bot -> run canary perf runs across regions and post numbers

perf-bot: Canary run queued: https://perf.redwood.dev/runs/1792. Summary: canary reduced median small-request latency by 28% in eu-west-1, p95 unchanged.

Jess: I'll draft the PR tonight, targeting canary tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

Maya: I'll own the router change, will sync with Jess re: interface.

Ravi: I'll spike KV-hash today, aim to have benchmark by EOD.

Alex: If we can't get fixes in by canary, do a rollback of the kernel-selection ordering. We can't ship a perf regression that breaks PLG. :eyes:

Jess: ack :shipit:

Maya: ack :thumbsup:

Ravi: taking it.

Alex: thx all — keeping thread for updates.
